changes_made.explanation: The paper does NOT address NLG tasks as its primary focus. It evaluates classification performance (response selection and addressee recognition) using LLMs. While summaries and descriptions are generated, they are used as input representations for classification evaluation, not as the main NLG outputs being evaluated.

The paper uses accuracy and conditional perplexity to evaluate classification tasks, not to evaluate generated NLG outputs. Since this is not an NLG evaluation paper, these metrics are not applicable to NLG evaluation.
No LLMs are used as judges to evaluate generated outputs. Llama2-13b-chat is used for classification tasks and generating summaries/descriptions, but not as an evaluator.
No human evaluation is conducted in this paper.

overall_notes: This paper is primarily about evaluating classification performance in multi-party conversations (response selection and addressee recognition) using LLMs. While it involves some text generation (summaries, descriptions), these are used as input representations for classification tasks, not as the main NLG outputs being evaluated. The paper focuses on diagnostic evaluation of model capabilities rather than NLG evaluation.
